settings.title: More than a
settings.intro: Mentoring isn't a lecture or a program to sit through. It's a real relationship built on trust, consistency, and showing up — week after week.

features.title: One-on-one matches
features.text: We pair each young person with a mentor chosen for shared interests and a compatible personality. No group sessions, no one-size-fits-all — just a real connection.

features.title: Weekly consistency
features.text: Mentors and mentees meet every week, in person or online, for a couple of hours. It's the steady rhythm that builds trust and lets real conversations happen.

features.title: Goal-setting together
features.text: Mentors help mentees set and reach goals — school, hobbies, confidence, or just figuring out the next step. Small wins stack into big momentum.

features.title: Family involvement
features.text: We keep parents and guardians in the loop with regular updates and family events, so the whole support network grows stronger together.

features.title: Life-skills workshops
features.text: Quarterly workshops on money, careers, communication, and wellbeing give mentees practical tools for the road ahead.

features.title: A community that lasts
features.text: Matches don't end at 18. Alumni stay connected through events and can become mentors themselves — the circle keeps growing.

settings.title: From first hello to
settings.intro: We take matching seriously — for the young person and the mentor. Here's how a relationship gets started and grows.

steps.title: Apply
steps.text: A family or a young person applies online, or a school refers them. It takes ten minutes and costs nothing.

steps.title: We get to know you
steps.text: Our team meets the young person and their family to understand their interests, needs, and what kind of mentor would be the best fit.

steps.title: We find the right mentor
steps.text: We match them with a vetted, trained volunteer whose personality and interests align. Both sides meet and decide together.

steps.title: The match grows
steps.text: Weekly meetings begin, supported by our coordinators. We check in regularly to make sure the relationship is thriving — and step in if it needs support.

settings.note: Most matches are up and running within six weeks of the first application. We don't rush a match — the right fit is worth the wait.

settings.title: Questions we
settings.intro: Straight answers about mentoring, matching, and how to get involved.

items.question: How much does mentoring cost for families?
items.answer: Nothing. Northstar Mentors is completely free for every family and young person. We're funded by donations, grants, and community partners — never by the families we serve.

items.question: Who can become a mentor?
items.answer: Any responsible adult 21 or older who can commit to one weekly meeting for at least a year. We look for reliability, empathy, and a genuine interest in young people — not any particular background or profession.

items.question: How are mentors vetted?
items.answer: Every mentor completes a thorough background check, multiple interviews, and a training program before being matched. We also check in with mentors and mentees regularly to keep every relationship safe and healthy.

items.question: What if a match isn't working?
items.answer: It happens, and it's not a failure. Our coordinators check in regularly and can adjust the match, provide extra support, or make a new pairing if needed. The young person's wellbeing always comes first.

items.question: Can I volunteer without being a full mentor?
items.answer: Yes. We need event helpers, workshop facilitators, and behind-the-scenes support too. If you're not ready to commit to a weekly match, there are plenty of other ways to help.
